review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp lemmas for direction, termination and competing rules. They are `complexifyPi_apply_ofReal`, `_apply_star`, `_zero`, `_add`, `_smul`, the series versions, and `complexifyPi_sum_ofReal` and `_sum_star`. None of them looks loop-prone or badly oriented. The non-simp `complexifyPi_apply` expands to a sum, so leaving it out of simp is reasonable. Two lower-confidence points remain. First, the additive interface covers `0`, `+` and `•` but not `-`. Second, the `(c : ℂ) • …` right-hand sides may compete with `Complex.coe_smul`. I did not run Lean, so I could not check whether `Complex.coe_smul` actually fires on `ContinuousMultilinearMap`/`FormalMultilinearSeries` scalars. A grep of the tauceti repo found no uses of these simp lemmas outside this file.

findings.excerpt:
theorem complexifyPi_add (g : ContinuousMultilinearMap ℝ (fun _ : ν ↦ ι → ℝ) ℝ) :
    (f + g).complexifyPi = f.complexifyPi + g.complexifyPi :=
findings.problem: The simp interface says that complexification is ℝ-linear and gives simp lemmas for `0`, `+` and `•`. It has no lemma for `-f` or `f - g`. The module doc advertises the `ℝ`-linearity lemmas as a set. `ContinuousMultilinearMap` and `FormalMultilinearSeries` both have `Neg` and `Sub`. So `(-f).complexifyPi` and `(f - g).complexifyPi` are stuck terms, and simp gets no further on expressions such as `(p - q).complexifyPi n`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] complexifyPi_neg` and `@[simp] complexifyPi_sub` for both `ContinuousMultilinearMap.complexifyPi` and `FormalMultilinearSeries.complexifyPi`. Prove them with the existing `eq_complexifyPi_of_forall_ofReal` and `ext1 n; simp` pattern. Alternatively, bundle complexification as an `ℝ`-linear map or `AddMonoidHom`, so that `map_neg` and `map_sub` apply.
findings.benefit: Differences of real series, such as `p - q` for a Taylor remainder, then complexify by `simp`. Users no longer have to prove the neg/sub identities by hand when they work with the `0`/`+`/`•` lemmas.

findings.excerpt: theorem complexifyPi_smul (c : ℝ) : (c • f).complexifyPi = (c : ℂ) • f.complexifyPi :=
findings.problem: The simp lemma's right-hand side has the form `(↑c : ℂ) • x`. Mathlib has the simp, norm_cast lemma `Complex.coe_smul : (x : ℂ) • y = x • y`, which rewrites that form to a real scalar action. If it fires on these structures, simp normalises the right-hand side again after using this lemma. The lemma then does not state its own normal form, and rewriting depends on how the two lemmas interact. If it does not fire, the real-scalar and complex-scalar forms stay separate and users may need both. I did not run Lean, so I could not check whether the instances unify.
findings.proposed_change: Check with `simp?` or the simpNF linter which form simp ends in. Then state the simp lemma in that form. Provide the other form as a non-simp lemma or as a `norm_cast` lemma, whichever matches the existing `Complex.coe_smul` behaviour. Apply the same change to the series version at line 272.
findings.benefit: A single canonical normal form for scalar multiples of complexified forms and series. It avoids two competing scalar-action forms in downstream simp calls.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem Complex.coe_smul {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℂ E] (x : ℝ) (y : E) :
    (x : ℂ) • y = x • y
